explanation.text:
(Pro. 19:1-29)

(Compare Pro 28:6). "Rich" for fool here. Integrity is better than riches (Pro 15:16-17; Pro 16:8).

bsb.text: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.

explanation.text: The last illustrates the first clause. Rashness, the result of ignorance, brings trouble.

bsb.text: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.

explanation.text: perverteth . . . way--turns him back from right (Pro 13:6; Jam 1:13); and he blames God for his failures.

bsb.text: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 14:20). Such facts are often adduced with implied disapprobation.

bsb.text: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.

explanation.text: Compare Pro 19:9, where perish explains not escape here (compare Psa 88:9-10).

bsb.text: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.

explanation.text:
Many will entreat the favour of the prince,.... Or of the liberal and bountiful man; as kings and princes generally are, Luke 22:25; such have many to wait upon them, and are humble petitioners to them. Aben Ezra and Gersom interpret the many of great and honourable men, who are courtiers to kings and princes; who wait upon them, ask favours of them, and seek for places under them. The Targum is,

"there are many that minister before a prince;''

he has many servants, and some of them nobles;

and every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts; or "to a man of gift": who has it in his power to give, and has a heart to it; who is both a rich man and a liberal man; who is both able and willing to communicate to the necessities of others: such a man not only has the poor his friends, but others will speak well of him, and will make application to him on account of the poor; and, for the sake of doing good to them, will court his friendship and acquaintance. Bayne interprets this "man of gift" of Christ, who ascended on high, and received gifts for men, and gives them to men.

bsb.text: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
All the brothers of a poor man hate him—how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.

explanation.text:
(Compare Margin; Pro 15:32).

loveth . . . soul--or, "himself," which he evinces by regarding his best interests.

keepeth--or, "regards."

bsb.text: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.

explanation.text:
A false witness shall not be unpunished,.... See Gill on Proverbs 19:5;

and he that speaketh lies shall perish; or "be lost", shall be undone for ever; he shall not enter into the holy city, but have his part in the lake of fire: they that speak lies in hypocrisy, doctrinal ones, and are given up to believe and profess them, such shall be damned, 2 Thessalonians 2:11.

bsb.text: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 17:7). The fool is incapable of properly using pleasure as knowledge, yet for him to have it is less incongruous than the undue elevation of servants. Let each abide in his calling (Co1 7:20).

bsb.text: Luxury is unseemly for a fool—how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 14:29; Pro 16:32). This inculcation of a forgiving spirit shows that true religion is always the same (Mat 5:22-24).

bsb.text: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 16:14-15; Pro 20:2). A motive to submission to lawful authority.

bsb.text: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.

explanation.text:
calamity--literally, "calamities," varied and many.

continual dropping--a perpetual annoyance, wearing out patience.

bsb.text: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.

explanation.text:
A contrast of men's gifts and God's, who, though author of both blessings, confers the latter by His more special providence.

and--or, "but," implying that the evils of Pro 19:13 are only avoided by His care.

bsb.text: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.

explanation.text:
a deep sleep--a state of utter indifference.

idle soul--or, "person" (compare Pro 10:4; Pro 12:24).

bsb.text: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:17; Pro 13:13).

despiseth . . . ways--opposed to keeping or observing, neglects (Pro 16:17) (as unworthy of regard) his moral conduct.

bsb.text: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 14:21; Psa 37:26).

hath pity--shown by acts (compare Margin).

bsb.text: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 13:24; Pro 23:13).

let not . . . spare--literally, "do not lift up thy soul" (Psa 24:4; Psa 25:1), that is, do not desire to his death; a caution to passionate parents against angry chastisement.

bsb.text: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.

explanation.text: Repeated efforts of kindness are lost on ill-natured persons.

bsb.text: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 13:18-20).

latter end-- (Pro 5:11). In youth prepare for age.

bsb.text: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 16:1, Pro 16:9; Psa 33:10-11). The failure of man's devices is implied.

bsb.text: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.

explanation.text: desire--that is, to do good, indicates a kind disposition (Pro 11:23); and the poor thus affected are better than liars, who say and do not.

bsb.text: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.

explanation.text:
The fear . . . life--(Compare Pro 3:2).

abide--or, "remain contented" (Ti1 4:8).

not visited with evil-- (Pro 10:3; Psa 37:25), as a judgment, in which sense visit is often used (Psa 89:32; Jer 6:15).

bsb.text: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.

explanation.text: bosom--literally, a wide dish in which the hand was plunged in eating (Mat 26:23). Compare Pro 26:15, the sentiment expressed with equal irony and less exaggeration.

bsb.text: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.

explanation.text: Such is the benefit of reproof; even the simple profit, much more the wise.

bsb.text: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.

explanation.text: Unfilial conduct often condemned (Pro 17:21-25; Pro 20:20; Deu 21:18, Deu 21:21).

bsb.text: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.

explanation.text: Avoid whatever leads from truth.

bsb.text: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.

explanation.text:
ungodly witness--(Compare Margin), one false by bad principles (compare Pro 6:12).

scorneth judgment--sets at naught the dictates of justice.

devoureth--literally, "swalloweth," as something delightful.

bsb.text: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity.

explanation.text:
Their punishment is sure, fixed, and ready (compare Pro 3:34; Pro 10:13).

bsb.text: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
